title: Regional speed camera processing centre and reserves
subtitle: Moody's credit rating, debenture plans, tax stabilization and working funds reserves, and community arts funding updates
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that the Region set up its own processing centre for automated speed enforcement tickets {{vote:m5}}. The centre supports Council's expansion of speed cameras to all school zones. Staff said Toronto's joint centre cannot keep up with the volume, so some infractions are not being processed. The staffing and budget needs will come forward in the 2024 budget. Council still has to adopt the recommendation.

The committee also received three finance reports for information: the fall 2023 debenture issuance preview, Moody's credit rating update, and the five-year history of the Tax stabilization and Working funds reserves. The Region keeps its AAA rating. Staff said that rating helps keep borrowing costs lower for the Region and for the area municipalities, which borrow through it.

Staff cautioned that using reserves only to hold down tax increases may not be sustainable. Under other business, staff said a report on arts funding will be part of the 2024 budget process, and the Union Co-operative item will return this fall as part of the budget. The committee then adjourned after a closed session was called.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Region establish its own processing centre, send the staffing and start-up budget through the 2024 budget, and amend the Redflex agreement to supply the equipment {{vote:m5}}.
The committee received for information the preview of the fall 2023 debenture issuance.
The committee received the Moody's credit rating update for information after it was pulled from the consent agenda for discussion.

decisions.item: Tax stabilization and working funds reserves
decisions.detail: The committee received for information the five-year continuity report on the Tax stabilization Reserve and Working Funds Reserve.

debate: On Moody's, councillors asked whether rising debt could cost the Region its AAA rating. Staff said debt burden alone would probably not do it, because the rating weighs many factors. Staff said Moody's mentions of Bill 23 and the review of two-tier government reflect uncertainty about future debt.

Councillors discussed reserves. One said reserves are routinely used to reduce tax increases, such as the planned gas price provision, and asked whether that would threaten the rating. Another favoured building reserves to protect the rating. Staff said a use of that size is unlikely to be significant against total reserves, but that using reserves only to cut the levy may push increases into later years.

On the processing centre, staff said the Toronto joint centre has capacity limits and a 23-day deadline to lay charges. A late vendor quote change raised one-time costs, which staff said program revenues would recover. Staff said Ottawa's centre is not an option because it is not open to joint processing.

One councillor was concerned about public backlash, citing past removal of speed cameras elsewhere, and about people being fined more for lesser offences. Staff said the focus is school zones where drivers go far over the limit, and that consistent province-wide rules protect the program's credibility. Other councillors supported the item on child safety grounds.

Staff said processing-centre jobs are entry-level with high turnover, and the Region is working with Toronto and its HR department on retention. Net revenue would go to a reserve to sustain the program as speeding falls and to fund small road safety improvements.
